decisions.executionNote: Begin elbow-up right-arm approach toward the single purple piece; rotate gradually toward a downward grasp while keeping left arm parked.
Finish vertical right gripper alignment and descend over purple star; verify centering before closing.
Small wrist-image centering correction, close fully around purple star, then lift vertically to check retention.
Purple star appears retained after lift. Carry it above the shortest, rightmost peg without crossing arms; keep gripper closed.
Correct star laterally over shortest peg and lower slowly toward insertion height; visual depth remains uncertain.
Peg is visible through star hole. Make a small centering and seating descent, release, then lift to inspect the placement.
Star did not seat and is tilted beside the peg. Withdraw open gripper vertically and allow it to settle before recovery.
Star has settled flat left of the shortest peg, not inserted. Reapproach its observed center for a more stable grasp.
Close on the centered flat star and lift vertically clear of neighboring pegs; inspect retention and hole offset.
The star stayed on the board and fingers closed empty. Reopen and descend farther to engage its sides, keeping the hole centered.
Open fingers appear blocked by adjacent pegs. Lift and turn the grasp axis ninety degrees so the fingers can approach from front and back.
Descend with front-back finger alignment to avoid neighboring pegs, straighten the wrist and close around the star.
Finish closing on star at the lower grasp height, then lift straight up for a retention check before peg alignment.
Star is tilted in the grasp. Move it clear of the pegs to reset it flat on the right-side table before attempting accurate insertion.
Star slipped and remains flat on the board. Recenter precisely at its new location with the front-back grasp axis.
Correct the front-back centering from wrist RGB, lower into a side grasp, and begin closing without lifting yet.
Allow closure to settle at the low grasp height, then perform a short vertical retention test.
Star now remains with the gripper after lift. Translate its offset hole over the shortest peg, then approach slowly while retaining it.
Lower star the remaining insertion distance and gently open the gripper, then inspect whether the shortest peg is seated through its hole.
Star is still beside the peg rather than inserted. Clear the fingers vertically to let it settle before correcting the forward offset.
The settled star is in front of the peg. Reorient to grasp from its free left and right sides rather than against the peg.
Lower open fingers to the star's side walls at its current front-of-board location, using a small lateral centering correction.
Wrist view shows the hole well forward of the grasp center. Move toward the robot to center it between the fingers, then close before lifting.
Lift the tilted star clear and carry it to free table space for a flat reset; verify it actually follows the closed fingers.
Star followed the gripper. Set it down in clear space and release to obtain a flat, stable regrasp away from the pegs.
Star has settled flat in clear space. Descend squarely to table-grasp height with fingers open, correcting the small lateral offset.
Center the flat star between the fingers at table height, close gradually, and test retention with a short lift.
The flat star appears retained. Lift clear, then carry its hole above the shortest peg using the observed grasp offset; keep closed.
Use the wrist view to remove the remaining lateral hole offset and lower toward the short peg, without releasing before checking alignment.
Contact tilted the star rather than inserting it. Lift slightly, correct the hole forward relative to the peg, and reapproach without opening.
Recenter the tilted star's hole over the peg using the head view, then release without pushing and lift clear so gravity can flatten it.
Clear the right fingers to let the star settle around the visible peg. Begin a gradual elbow-up left-arm approach to the leftmost blue piece.
Star appears settled on its peg. Approach the leftmost blue rectangle with the left arm and the right yellow square with the right, staying in separate workspaces.
Refine both table grasps from wrist centering: blue rectangle with left fingers aligned to its sides, yellow square with right fingers rotated to its edges.
Center the blue rectangle, close both grippers fully on the piece sides, and lift vertically to verify retention before transport.
Both pieces visibly followed the lift. Carry blue above the leftmost peg and yellow toward the third peg, maintaining separated arms and clearance above peg tips.
Refine hole positions above their respective pegs and begin a cautious descent. Keep both pieces held until peg engagement is visible.
The wrist housings became too close. Separate the right arm with yellow retained, then continue blue placement alone with restored downward alignment.
The first peg tip is visible through the blue hole. Lower the blue piece slowly along the peg while the right arm holds yellow safely clear.
Blue is behind the peg rather than threaded. Lift clear, shift its hole toward the robot and slightly right, then approach the peg tip again.
The blue hole now overlaps the peg tip. Apply a millimeter lateral correction and descend slowly to test threading, keeping yellow stationary.
Blue tilted on contact, so threading was not achieved. Lift clear and compensate the remaining forward grasp offset before another visual alignment check.
Blue remains tilted within the grasp. Counter-rotate the wrist while compensating the gripper-tip position, aiming to flatten the piece above the peg before insertion.
Lower the reoriented blue cautiously toward the peg; bring the retained yellow part closer while keeping wrist housings separated.
Make a small blue hole correction toward the visible peg tip and lower cautiously. Align yellow above the third peg while maintaining wrist separation.
Blue has tipped again; lift it clear instead of forcing insertion. Correct yellow's hole left and toward the robot, then lower over its peg while keeping it flat.
Yellow's hole overlaps the peg tip. Make a small final centering correction, release gently rather than forcing the tilt, and lift clear to inspect seating.
Yellow visibly seated on its peg after release. Withdraw the right arm and bring the retained blue hole back above the first peg with clearance.
Shift blue forward over the first peg, release gently to remove grasp-induced tilt, and lift clear to inspect where it settles.
Blue fell beside the first peg. Prioritize the remaining yellow square: return left wrist downward and approach it while moving right arm clear for a center transfer.
Lower the left open gripper squarely around the remaining yellow piece, correcting small pitch and position errors before grasping.
Close on the centered yellow square and lift it straight up; keep right arm clear while checking the grasp.
Yellow is retained. Carry it above clear front-center table space for a staged transfer to the right arm without crossing the arms.
Set the yellow square down at front center, open the left gripper, and begin lifting clear before the right arm approaches for transfer.
Yellow rests in the center staging area. Withdraw the left arm upward and left before bringing the right arm toward the transfer, maintaining separation.
Approach the staged yellow with the right arm, accounting for its offset from link6, while the left arm moves above a separate blue piece. Keep both grippers open.
Lower the right open gripper around the staged yellow square. Hold the left arm clear while verifying the transfer grasp alignment.
Fine-center the staged yellow, close the right gripper fully, and lift to verify retention before carrying it to the yellow stack.
Carry retained yellow above its stack, compensating the observed hole offset. Independently align and lower the left gripper around the next blue rectangle.
Fine-center and grasp the blue rectangle, then test retention. Shift yellow forward over its stack and descend gradually, keeping its gripper closed.
